historical_claims.anchor: Octavia Butler was born in Pasadena, California, in 1947.
Her father died when she was young, and her mother worked as a domestic employee.
The Huntington Library's exhibition of her papers documents the notebooks, photographs, and working habits behind that persistence.
In a 2004 interview with Joshunda Sanders, Butler recalled researching Kindred through slave narratives, historical studies, and writings by the wives of plantation owners
She also discussed her decision to begin in 1976, the United States bicentennial year.
The novel was published in 1979, after the civil-rights movement had changed law and public life, and amid ongoing conflicts over inequality, memory, and the interpretation of American history.

description: Analyzes Octavia E. Butler’s Kindred through Dana’s involuntary journeys from bicentennial California to Maryland under slavery, her dependence on Rufus and Alice’s family history, and the unequal options available to Dana and Kevin. Examines constrained survival, bodily autonomy, literacy, the limits of historical empathy, the incomplete archive and the permanent injury and the unresolved fates of people she knew.
